title: Kiwi Know-How
subject: Social Sciences
source: New Zealand places, people and history

questions.q: What is the capital city of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Wellington is the capital, where Parliament meets. Auckland is our biggest city.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Aoraki / Mount Cook in the Southern Alps is the highest at about 3,724 m.

questions.q: In which year was Te Tiriti o Waitangi first signed?
questions.explanation: Te Tiriti o Waitangi was first signed on 6 February 1840 at Waitangi.

questions.q: What is New Zealand's longest river?
questions.explanation: The Waikato River is the longest, at about 425 km.

questions.q: What is the North Island called in te reo Māori?
questions.explanation: Te Ika-a-Māui means "the fish of Māui", from the story of Māui fishing up the land.

questions.q: Rakiura is the te reo Māori name for…
questions.explanation: Rakiura is Stewart Island, at the bottom of the South Island.

questions.q: In 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country to…
options: Let women vote in national elections
questions.explanation: In 1893 women in New Zealand won the right to vote in national elections — a world first.

questions.q: Who led the campaign for women to vote in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Kate Sheppard led the petition that helped women win the vote in 1893. She is on the $10 note.

options: The Māori New Year, when a star cluster rises
The end of the school year
questions.explanation: Matariki is the Māori New Year, marked by the rising of the Matariki star cluster in winter.

questions.q: Which of these is an official language of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Te reo Māori and New Zealand Sign Language are official languages by law.

questions.q: What is the sea between New Zealand and Australia called?
questions.explanation: The Tasman Sea separates New Zealand and Australia.

questions.q: With Tenzing Norgay, who was first to climb Mount Everest in 1953?
questions.explanation: Sir Edmund Hillary from Auckland and Tenzing Norgay reached the top of Everest in 1953.

questions.q: What money do we use in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: New Zealand uses the New Zealand dollar (NZD).

questions.q: True or false: Waitangi Day is on 6 February.
questions.explanation: Waitangi Day remembers the first signing of Te Tiriti o Waitangi on 6 February 1840.

questions.q: Which is New Zealand's biggest city by population?
questions.explanation: Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland has the most people of any NZ city.
